abstract: De novo protein design often produces thermostable proteins that denature above 100 {degrees}C, which complicates the analysis of their stability. Thermostable proteins can be unfolded by combined chemical and thermal denaturation followed by global analysis of multiple melting curves. Here, we have developed CheMelt, a new online tool for global analysis of unfolding data via an intuitive graphical user interface. We use nanoscale differential scanning fluorimetry followed by CheMelt data analysis to dissect the combined thermal and chemical denaturation of thirty-five de novo designed protein binders. Thirteen present sufficient fluorescence changes to extract thermodynamic parameters of unfolding. These de novo designed proteins have systematically lower {Delta}Cp and m-values than comparable natural proteins. We show that a high thermostability of a designed protein does not necessarily imply a high equilibrium stability, and demonstrate the potential of CheMelt in dissecting thermodynamic properties for protein design and engineering. CheMelt can be accessed at https://spc.embl-hamburg.de/app/chemelt
